entry.englishMeaning: a fair assumption that someone acted honestly when the facts are uncertain
entry.coreIdea: Withhold blame while the facts remain uncertain.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Idiomatic phrase for choosing a fair or favourable interpretation when the facts are uncertain.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Positive toward fairness and restraint, without asserting that the person is innocent.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Cautious and fair-minded here: the speaker withholds judgement until hearing an explanation.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Common in everyday and professional discussions of disputed behaviour. It means provisional trust, not ignoring contrary evidence.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: I will give him the benefit of the doubt until we hear his explanation.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: a fair assumption that someone acted honestly when the facts are uncertain
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The speaker will provisionally assume that the man acted honestly until his explanation is available.

when_to_use: Choose a fair interpretation of someone's behaviour when you do not yet have enough evidence to judge it.
when_not_to_use: Do not use it to dismiss clear contrary evidence; the fairness is provisional, not unconditional belief.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: give someone the benefit of the doubt
common_collocations: give her the benefit of the doubt
deserve the benefit of the doubt

examples.example_1: I will give him the benefit of the doubt until we hear his explanation.
examples.example_2: The parcel arrived damaged, but I gave the courier the benefit of the doubt because I had not seen how it was packed.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: She did not reply to our invitation.
B: Let us give her the benefit of the doubt; she may not have received it.
A: I will check before assuming she ignored us.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: Give him benefit of doubt.
mistakes_differences.correction: Say: Give him the benefit of the doubt. Keep both instances of the in the fixed expression.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: The benefit of the doubt is provisional fairness under uncertainty; proof of innocence is evidence establishing that someone was not responsible.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Leave the verdict open until the missing facts arrive.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: Give her the benefit of the doubt until we know what happened.
memory_practice.recall_question: What uncertainty makes giving someone the benefit of the doubt reasonable?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: Wait for an explanation before blaming someone. B: Ignore conclusive evidence against them. Which better fits this expression?
memory_practice.production_task: Respond fairly to a colleague's unexplained lateness using benefit of the doubt, and name a fact you would check.

advanced_nuance: Giving someone the benefit of the doubt does not mean being convinced they acted correctly. It is a choice not to adopt the less favourable interpretation while the evidence remains incomplete.

entry.pronunciation: Approximate pronunciation: moov tuh DYE-uh-log. Capitals show stress; this is text guidance, not audio.
entry.englishMeaning: to shift an interaction toward an open and constructive exchange of views
entry.coreIdea: Change the interaction into a constructive exchange.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract phrase for changing an interaction into an open exchange; here, Yvonne intends to begin a more constructive conversation with Jotham.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Positive in this passage: dialogue is presented as a preferable way of interacting.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Tentative and purposeful here: “going to try” expresses an intention without guaranteeing success.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Natural in discussion of communication methods, though “start an open conversation” may be clearer in everyday speech.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Yvonne  is  going  to  try  to  move  to  dialogue  with  Jotham.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: to shift an interaction toward an open and constructive exchange of views
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: Yvonne intends to try to start an open exchange with Jotham. The sentence describes her intention, not a successful outcome.

when_to_use: Describe a shift from confrontation, avoidance or one-sided statements toward an exchange where both people can contribute.
when_not_to_use: If one person only delivers instructions and refuses replies, do not describe that alone as moving to dialogue.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: move to dialogue with + person; move from confrontation to dialogue
common_collocations: move to dialogue with the other side

examples.example_1: We need to move to dialogue with the residents before deciding how to use the hall.
examples.example_2: After weeks of angry messages, the two groups agreed to move to dialogue.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: We keep repeating our positions without listening.
B: Let us move to dialogue and ask what each side needs.
A: I will explain my concern, then hear yours.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Mistake: Calling a one-sided lecture a move to dialogue merely because someone is speaking.
mistakes_differences.correction: To move to dialogue, create space for the other person to explain and respond as well.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Move to dialogue describes a change in how people interact; reach agreement describes a possible outcome that dialogue does not guarantee.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Two opposing speeches become a conversation with turns for both people.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: We can move to dialogue by asking each person to explain their concern.
memory_practice.recall_question: Does moving to dialogue guarantee that both people will agree?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: Invite each side to explain and question. B: Repeat a demand while refusing replies. Which moves toward dialogue?
memory_practice.production_task: Write an invitation to move to dialogue after a disagreement, specifying how both people will get a chance to speak.

advanced_nuance: Move to dialogue is purposeful communication-method language rather than a fixed idiom. Start an open conversation is often plainer. In either wording, the shift concerns the interaction, not guaranteed agreement.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract compound for a cause of delay; here, the missing signature prevents progress.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Negative about the obstruction, but often less severe than a permanent failure.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Matter-of-fact and focused here: “only” identifies one remaining obstacle.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Common conversational and workplace English. “Cause of the delay” is clearer in formal writing; this is not the robbery sense.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: The missing signature is the only hold-up.
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The missing signature is the remaining reason the process cannot move forward.

when_to_use: Name a delay or the obstacle causing it in everyday planning and work.
when_not_to_use: For a final cancellation, say cancellation rather than implying that work is merely delayed by a hold-up.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: a hold-up in + process; the hold-up is + obstacle; cause a hold-up

examples.example_1: The missing signature is the only hold-up.
examples.example_2: A hold-up at the ticket desk meant we missed the start of the film.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Why has the order not been sent?
B: There is a hold-up with the address confirmation.
A: I will check the details now.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: The missing signature is hold-up.
mistakes_differences.correction: Say: The missing signature is a hold-up, or the only hold-up. The singular countable noun needs a determiner.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: A hold-up delays progress; a cancellation ends the planned activity rather than merely postponing it.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: A document waits at one blocked step in the process.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: The address check is the only hold-up.
memory_practice.recall_question: What obstacle is causing the hold-up in the source?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: An order waits for a missing signature. B: An order is delivered on time. Which involves a hold-up?
memory_practice.production_task: Explain a hold-up in an invented delivery and state the next step needed to remove it.

advanced_nuance: Hold-up is conversational and can name either the delay or its cause. It also has a separate robbery sense, so naming the process—such as a hold-up in delivery—makes this delay meaning clearer.

entry.tamilMeaning: தானே ஒழுக்கத்தில் மற்றவர்களைவிட உயர்ந்தவர் என்று கருதுகிற
entry.englishMeaning: convinced that one’s own behaviour or beliefs are morally superior
entry.coreIdea: Act as though your moral judgement makes you superior.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract adjective for believing one's own conduct or beliefs are morally superior to other people's.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Strongly negative: it criticizes perceived moral superiority rather than ordinary confidence.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Concerned about the listener's impression here: the question asks how to avoid sounding superior while raising a complaint.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Common in commentary and personal criticism, but a strong label. Describe the behaviour more specifically in diplomatic feedback.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Is  there  a  way  to  talk  to  your  neighbors  about  their  annoying  behavior  and  not  come  across  as  self-rig hteous  or  demanding?
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: convinced that one’s own behaviour or beliefs are morally superior
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The speaker wants to raise a complaint without appearing morally superior to the neighbours.

when_to_use: Criticise an attitude of moral superiority, especially when someone appears certain that only their own conduct is right.
when_not_to_use: Do not equate every firm moral objection with self-righteousness; the criticism concerns the superior attitude, not merely having principles.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: sound / seem / come across as + self-righteous; a self-righteous + tone / lecture

examples.example_1: His self-righteous lecture made it hard to discuss the actual problem.
examples.example_2: She wanted to ask the neighbours to lower the music without sounding self-righteous.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: I told them that decent people would never behave like that.
B: That can sound self-righteous. Could you explain how the noise affects you instead?
A: I will focus on the behaviour and its effect.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Mistake: Using self-righteous as praise for someone who simply behaves ethically.
mistakes_differences.correction: Use self-righteous to criticise perceived moral superiority; use principled when you intend to praise consistent ethical conduct.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Principled can praise commitment to values; self-righteous criticises an attitude that one's own moral position makes one superior.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: A raised finger and a lecture implying that only the speaker is decent.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: I can raise the concern without giving a self-righteous lecture.
memory_practice.recall_question: What attitude does self-righteous criticise beyond having strong beliefs?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: Explain a concern while listening respectfully. B: Declare that only you have proper morals. Which sounds self-righteous?
memory_practice.production_task: Rewrite a fictional morally superior complaint as a specific, respectful request. Explain how the rewrite avoids sounding self-righteous.

advanced_nuance: Self-righteous is a strong judgement about someone's attitude. In a constructive complaint, describing the particular words or behaviour may be more useful than applying this label to the person.

entry.pronunciation: Approximate pronunciation: un-TY-mlee DETH. Capitals show stress; this is text guidance, not audio.
entry.englishMeaning: death happening earlier than expected or natural
entry.coreIdea: A death is regarded as happening too soon.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Established phrase for a death regarded as occurring too soon, before an expected lifespan or appropriate time.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Sad or tragic association: it emphasizes the premature loss rather than giving a medical cause.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Relief is suggested by “Saved from,” although the brief fragment does not establish the wider emotional setting.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Relatively formal or literary, common in tributes and narratives. “Premature death” is more clinical.

meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: death happening earlier than expected or natural
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: Saved from indicates that an early death was avoided. The fragment alone does not establish the exact danger or wider circumstances.

when_to_use: Describe a death regarded as premature in a narrative, remembrance or tribute.
when_not_to_use: Do not treat untimely death as an explanation of the medical cause or the precise age involved.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: an untimely death; mourn someone's untimely death; saved from an untimely death

examples.example_1: The novel begins with the untimely death of a young musician.
examples.example_2: The villagers mourned the teacher's untimely death.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Why does the tribute call her death untimely?
B: It presents her untimely death as a loss that came far too soon.
A: It does not explain the cause, though.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Mistake: Assuming untimely death identifies a particular cause of death.
mistakes_differences.correction: Untimely death says that the loss occurred too soon; name the cause separately only when it is established and relevant.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Untimely death emphasises premature loss; sudden death emphasises how unexpectedly or rapidly it occurred. Those descriptions can overlap but are not identical.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: A life story ends while much still seemed to lie ahead.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: The tribute remembered the work she completed before her untimely death.
memory_practice.recall_question: Does untimely death identify the cause or express that the loss came too soon?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: A tribute emphasises a life cut short. B: A report lists a precise cause without discussing timing. Which directly explains untimely?
memory_practice.production_task: Write one respectful sentence about a fictional character's untimely death, without inventing a medical explanation.

advanced_nuance: Untimely death is evaluative and often mournful: it presents the loss as too early. It does not define a fixed age threshold, and its relatively formal tone suits tributes and narratives.

entry.pronunciation: Approximate pronunciation: out-LAN-dish. Capitals show stress; this is text guidance, not audio.
entry.coreIdea: So extreme or unusual that it seems hard to accept.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract adjective for claims judged extremely unusual or unreasonable.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Negative here: it casts the claims as excessive and hard to accept.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Self-critical here: the speaker includes outlandish claims among their own argumentative mistakes.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Expressive vocabulary in speech and commentary. “Unsupported” is more precise if the actual problem is lack of evidence.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: I  spoke  in  absolutes,  only  pointed  out  fa cts  that  supported  my  view ,  and then  ended  with  a  list  of  outlandish  clai ms.
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The writer criticises their own exaggerated or unreasonable claims as part of a poor argument.

when_to_use: Describe a claim, suggestion or idea you judge extremely unusual, exaggerated or unreasonable.
when_not_to_use: If the only problem is missing evidence, unsupported may be more precise than the stronger judgement outlandish.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: an outlandish + claim / idea / suggestion; seem / sound + outlandish

examples.example_1: He made the outlandish claim that the whole project could be finished in an hour.
examples.example_2: At first, turning the abandoned station into a theatre sounded like an outlandish idea.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: She says we can double attendance without changing anything.
B: That sounds outlandish. What evidence supports it?
A: Let us ask before accepting the prediction.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Mistake: Using outlandish as a neutral synonym for slightly different.
mistakes_differences.correction: Use outlandish when you mean strikingly unusual or unreasonable; different alone does not carry that strong judgement.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Unconventional means outside the usual approach; outlandish is stronger and often suggests that the idea is excessive or difficult to believe.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: An enormous claim towers over the small amount of supporting evidence.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: We questioned the outlandish promise of instant success.
memory_practice.recall_question: Does outlandish sound neutral or express a strong reaction to an idea?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: A small change to a familiar schedule. B: A promise to complete a year's work in one afternoon. Which sounds outlandish?
memory_practice.production_task: Describe an invented outlandish project claim and ask one specific question that would test it.

advanced_nuance: Outlandish expresses the speaker's judgement, not proof of falsity. An idea can initially seem outlandish and later become workable; factual criticism should still identify what is unreasonable or unsupported.

entry.pronunciation: Approximate pronunciation: EEVZ-drop. Capitals show stress; this is text guidance, not audio.
entry.englishMeaning: to secretly listen to a private conversation
entry.coreIdea: Listen to a private conversation without openly joining it.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Literal verb for listening secretly to a private conversation, used here as a narrative invitation to observe an intimate discussion.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Often negative because it suggests intrusion, though the writer is using it to introduce an example rather than confess actual spying.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Inviting and slightly playful here: “We'll” brings the reader into the coming scene.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Common general vocabulary. In professional descriptions, “observe a sample conversation” avoids implying a privacy intrusion.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: We 'll  eavesdrop  on  a  couple  as  they  try  to  discuss  one  of  the  most  delicate  of  topics-p hysical  intima cy.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: to secretly listen to a private conversation
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The writer invites readers to observe a couple's private discussion as a narrative example. The wording does not establish actual covert listening by the reader.

when_to_use: Describe secretly listening to a conversation not intended for you, or a deliberate narrative imitation of that position.
when_not_to_use: If you accidentally hear a few words without trying to listen, overhear is usually more accurate.

examples.example_1: It was rude of him to eavesdrop on the conversation at the next table.
examples.example_2: The narrator lets readers eavesdrop on a fictional family's private discussion.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Did you hear what they were saying behind the door?
B: No. I did not want to eavesdrop.
A: We can ask them if there is anything we need to know.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: He tried to eavesdrop their conversation.
mistakes_differences.correction: Say: He tried to eavesdrop on their conversation. Use on before the people or conversation.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Eavesdrop generally implies intentional secret listening; overhear can describe hearing something unintentionally.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Someone leans toward a private conversation they were not invited to join.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: I did not want to eavesdrop on their private discussion.
memory_practice.recall_question: What usually distinguishes eavesdrop from accidentally overhear?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: Deliberately listen behind a door. B: Unexpectedly hear a loud remark while walking past. Which more clearly means eavesdrop?
memory_practice.production_task: Write two sentences contrasting an accidental overhearing with a decision not to eavesdrop further.

advanced_nuance: Eavesdrop often suggests a privacy intrusion, but writers can use it figuratively to position readers close to fictional private dialogue. That narrative invitation should not be mistaken for a factual claim of spying.

entry.tamilMeaning: முந்தைய நிகழ்வால் ஏற்படும் மறைமுக தொடர் விளைவு
entry.englishMeaning: an indirect consequence caused by an earlier event
entry.coreIdea: One event indirectly affects something further along.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Figurative phrase for a secondary consequence that follows from an earlier event, like one impact causing another.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Neutral by itself, though this sentence presents a delay spreading into training as an unwelcome effect.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Explanatory here: it links the delivery problem with a later impact on training.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Common in British and international workplace English. “Indirect consequence” is more formal and explicit.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: The late delivery had a knock-on effect on training.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: an indirect consequence caused by an earlier event
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The delivery delay affected training afterward, for example by changing when the training could happen. The quotation does not specify the exact change.

when_to_use: Explain how an initial event produces a secondary consequence in another activity or stage.
when_not_to_use: Do not call two unrelated problems a knock-on effect merely because they happen at similar times; show the causal link.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: have a knock-on effect on + activity; a knock-on effect of + initial event

examples.example_1: The late delivery had a knock-on effect on training.
examples.example_2: Longer library opening hours had a positive knock-on effect on attendance at evening clubs.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Why has training moved to Thursday?
B: The equipment arrived late, which had a knock-on effect on the schedule.
A: I will notify the participants.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: The delay had a knock-on effect to training.
mistakes_differences.correction: Say: The delay had a knock-on effect on training. Use on for what is affected.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: A direct effect follows immediately from the action itself; a knock-on effect emphasises a secondary consequence passed on to something else.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: One falling domino knocks over the next.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: The delivery delay had a knock-on effect on the launch.
memory_practice.recall_question: What link connects the original event to its knock-on effect?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: A missing part delays assembly, which delays training. B: An unrelated rainstorm occurs that day. Which describes a knock-on effect of the missing part?
memory_practice.production_task: Explain a three-step chain in which one project delay has a knock-on effect on another team's work.

advanced_nuance: Knock-on effect is often used for problems, but the consequence can be positive. Naming the direction and affected activity makes the phrase more informative than simply saying there were effects.

entry.englishMeaning: to make a noticeable difference to an important result
entry.coreIdea: Make a noticeable difference to a result that matters.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Figurative idiom for producing a noticeable change in an important measure, as though moving a gauge's needle.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Positive in this example: the desired changes would improve customer satisfaction.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Results-focused and advisory here: “should focus” urges attention to changes with a meaningful effect.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Common business jargon. “Make a measurable difference” is clearer for audiences unfamiliar with the idiom.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: We should focus on changes that move the needle on customer satisfaction.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: to make a noticeable difference to an important result
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The speaker recommends prioritising changes that noticeably improve customer satisfaction rather than changes with little impact.

when_to_use: Discuss whether an action makes a meaningful difference to an important outcome or measure.
when_not_to_use: For effort alone, use work hard or make changes; those actions do not necessarily move the needle on the desired result.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: move the needle on + outcome; do little / fail to move the needle

examples.example_1: We should focus on changes that move the needle on customer satisfaction.
examples.example_2: The new reminders did little to move the needle on attendance.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: We changed the button colour again.
B: Did that move the needle on completed bookings?
A: Not noticeably. Clearer instructions may have more impact.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Mistake: Saying work moved the needle merely because it took a lot of effort.
mistakes_differences.correction: Use move the needle when there is a noticeable difference in the relevant result, not simply more activity.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Make an effort describes input; move the needle describes impact on an outcome.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: A gauge finally shifts after a useful change.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: Clearer instructions could move the needle on completed applications.
memory_practice.recall_question: What outcome must you examine before claiming that a change moved the needle?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: Many cosmetic changes with no noticeable effect. B: A change that clearly improves completion. Which moves the needle on completion?
memory_practice.production_task: Name a small change that might move the needle on a workplace result, and say how you would check its effect.

advanced_nuance: Move the needle is business jargon and does not specify how large or lasting the effect is. Name the measure and the size of the change when precision matters; the idiom alone does not establish causation.

entry.pronunciation: Approximate pronunciation: KOM-plih-kay-tid. Capitals show stress; this is text guidance, not audio.
entry.englishMeaning: involving many connected parts and therefore difficult to understand or solve
entry.coreIdea: Many connected parts make the problem hard to understand or solve.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract description of a problem with many connected parts that make it difficult to understand or solve.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Often mildly negative because it highlights difficulty, without implying that the problem is impossible.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Explanatory here: the adjective establishes the kind of quality problem being discussed.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Common neutral vocabulary in everyday and professional English. It does not automatically mean that someone has made the problem unnecessarily difficult.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: For  example,  you're  talk ing  with  a  group  of  supervi sors  about  a  complicated  quality problem.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: involving many connected parts and therefore difficult to understand or solve
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The supervisors are discussing a quality problem with interrelated features that make it difficult to work through.

when_to_use: Describe an issue, explanation or arrangement with many connected details that create difficulty.
when_not_to_use: A task that requires great physical effort but has few steps may be hard without being complicated.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: a complicated + problem / process; complicated by + additional factor; too complicated to + action

examples.example_1: The team drew a diagram to explain the complicated approval process.
examples.example_2: Arranging transport became complicated because everyone arrived at a different time.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Why can we not fix the problem with one change?
B: It is complicated: changing the temperature also affects two later stages.
A: Let us map those connections first.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Mistake: Assuming complicated always means impossible to solve.
mistakes_differences.correction: A complicated problem may be solvable once its connected parts are understood and handled in order.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Difficult describes a broad range of challenges; complicated specifically suggests many details or connected parts that make something difficult.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Untangle several linked threads one connection at a time.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: A diagram helped us understand the complicated process.
memory_practice.recall_question: Can a simple task be difficult without being complicated?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A: Lifting one heavy box. B: Coordinating several linked schedules and permissions. Which is more clearly complicated?
memory_practice.production_task: Describe a complicated process from an invented project and explain which two parts depend on each other.

advanced_nuance: Complicated does not necessarily mean unnecessarily complex. Overcomplicated adds the judgement that avoidable detail has made something harder; the source adjective alone does not assign that blame.
